question: Assume today is 2026-09-12. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of passengers at London Heathrow Airport in September 2026, as reported in Heathrow's monthly traffic statistics.

target.what: Total passengers passing through London Heathrow Airport (LHR) during the calendar month of September 2026, as reported in Heathrow's monthly traffic statistics (total terminal passengers, all domestic and international, arriving and departing, including transfers counted per Heathrow's standard met
target.publisher: Heathrow Airport Limited (monthly traffic statistics / operational figures)
target.caveats: Target period is future/ongoing relative to the 2026-09-12 cutoff, so no September 2026 actual exists; must be forecast. Heathrow reports 'passengers' as terminal passengers (enplaned+deplaned, transfers included per its convention); alternative interpretations include excluding transfer passengers

candidates.perspective: Airport operator's published monthly traffic series
candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 passengers ≈ September 2025 passengers scaled by recent year-on-year growth trend observed in months published before cutoff (Jan–Aug 2026 vs 2025). Own history gives the seasonal level and the growth rate to extrapolate.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow monthly total passenger figures for September 2024 and September 2025, plus all 2025 and 2026 monthly totals published on or before 2026-09-12 (to compute YoY growth and seasonality). Minimum: Sept 2025 total and latest 2026 monthly YoY growth.

candidates.perspective: UK Civil Aviation Authority / ONS airport passenger data
candidates.hypothesis: CAA monthly airport statistics for Heathrow provide an independent, consistent passenger series that can cross-check and fill Heathrow's own reported totals; September 2026 can be built from CAA 2025 September level times growth.
candidates.data_to_find: CAA airport data for Heathrow: monthly terminal passengers Sept 2024, Sept 2025, and 2026 months available before cutoff. Substitute: ONS/Department for Transport airport passenger series.
search_hints: CAA Heathrow airport passenger statistics monthly

candidates.hypothesis: Passengers ≈ available seats × load factor × (1 + transfer share adjustment). September 2026 seat capacity at LHR from schedules (OAG/Cirium) times achieved load factor gives a bottom-up estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: LHR scheduled seat capacity for September 2026 (OAG/Cirium/airline schedules), and recent LHR load factors or Heathrow-reported seat occupancy. Minimum: September 2026 weekly seats and a load factor estimate.

candidates.perspective: Airport operational constraint (passenger cap / slot coordination)
candidates.hypothesis: Heathrow's passenger cap and runway slot limits bound monthly throughput; if demand exceeds cap, September 2026 passengers approach the cap-implied monthly maximum. Cap × days × utilisation gives an upper bound.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow annual passenger cap (e.g., 80–82 million) and any 2026 cap changes; daily runway movement limits and average passengers per movement. Minimum: current cap and average pax per ATM.
search_hints: Heathrow runway slots daily limit passengers

candidates.hypothesis: Heathrow's own annual passenger guidance/traffic forecasts for 2026, and IATA/ACI Europe forecasts, constrain the annual total; September is a share of the year. Annual forecast × September seasonal share ≈ target.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow 2026 annual passenger guidance or forecast (from results/investor releases before cutoff), and September's historical share of annual passengers. Minimum: 2026 annual guidance and Sept share.

candidates.perspective: Disruption, strikes, and demand events affecting September 2026
candidates.hypothesis: Known events before cutoff (strikes, ATC disruptions, weather, route launches/closures, economic conditions) shift September 2026 away from trend; quantify exposure to adjust the trend-based estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: Announced strikes/disruptions at LHR or UK ATC affecting September 2026; new route launches or airline capacity changes at LHR for autumn 2026. Minimum: any confirmed material disruption or capacity change.

candidates.hypothesis: September's share of annual passengers is stable across years; applying the historical September share to a 2026 annual estimate yields the monthly figure. Provides a cross-check on trend extrapolation.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow annual passenger totals and September monthly totals for 2015–2025 to compute September share and its variability. Minimum: 3–5 years of Sept share.
search_hints: Heathrow monthly passengers seasonal share September

candidates.perspective: Air transport movements and average passengers per movement
candidates.hypothesis: Passengers = air transport movements (ATMs) × average passengers per ATM. September 2026 ATMs from schedule/coordination data times recent pax-per-ATM gives an independent estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: LHR monthly ATMs for Sept 2025 and 2026 (schedule/coordination), and average passengers per ATM at LHR recently. Minimum: Sept 2026 ATMs and pax/ATM.

July 2026 7.9 million, down 1.5% YoY — the key recent growth signal before cutoff.

kept.name: September 2026 YoY growth factor vs September 2025
kept.rationale: Anchored on kept 2026 evidence: Jan–Aug cumulative -0.4% (p175), July -1.5% (p17), August -2.1% (p171), H1 +0.2% (p55). The trend decelerates into late summer, so September sits slightly below flat; range spans mild recovery to continued decline.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 behaves like the recent Jul–Aug 2026 run-rate rather than reverting to H1 strength.

kept.name: Net share of September 2026 passengers lost to the 8–9 Sep NATS outage
kept.rationale: Outage grounded 30% of Tuesday and 5% of Wednesday UK departures (p110, p111) against a normal 1–2% (p185, p186); ~2,000 UK flights affected (p109). kept.applies_when: The outage's LHR-specific cancellations are not fully recovered within September.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that LHR cancellations exceeded ~5% of monthly flights or that rebooking was negligible.

kept.name: September share of annual passengers, 2026 capacity/growth adjusted
kept.rationale: September is a shoulder month: 7.348m of 84.4m in 2025 ≈ 8.7%. Applied to a 2026 annual level near 84.3m (rolling 12m p176) with a small downward adjustment for the negative summer trend.

residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
